title: When the Gravity Breaks
premise: Quentin Yarrow has spent eleven years alone tending Earth's last seed vault, broadcasting maintenance logs to a colony world that stopped answering. When the ship Meridian returns from deep space carrying a crew who have aged backward into their own pasts, Quentin discovers they carry a message that could end the war between Earth and the colonies — but only if it reaches the right hands before both sides weaponize the time-reversal technology that made them. As factions hunt the crew and Quentin's own memories begin to unravel, he learns the message was encoded in his mind years ago by the woman he loved, making him the final courier. In the vault's deepest chamber, Quentin must choose to broadcast the truth — erasing his own identity in the process — and the war ends not with victory but with shared grief.
about_author: Sebastian Montrose is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing obsolete agricultural data before turning to fiction. He writes quiet, melancholy science fiction about people left behind by progress.

chapters.title: The Last Gardener
chapters.summary: Quentin Yarrow records his 4,000th daily log in the Svalbard seed vault, tending crops under artificial light for an Earth emptied by emigration. His transmissions to the colony of Meridian go unanswered. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: lonely devotion masking grief over the colony's silence and the lover he left behind.

chapters.title: A Light in the Ice
chapters.summary: Quentin detects an unregistered descent burning through the Arctic night. He treks across the ice and finds the ship Meridian crashed, its hull scarred by weapons fire no one on Earth possesses anymore. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into dread as he realizes the ship is from the colony that forgot him.

chapters.title: Children in Old Uniforms
chapters.summary: Inside the wreck, Quentin finds the crew alive but impossibly young — adults aged backward decades, including Commander Ilsa Voss, who should be seventy but appears twenty-five. They remember futures that haven't happened yet. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: uncanny horror mixed with recognition; one child-faced officer calls him by name.

chapters.title: What Voss Remembers
chapters.summary: Commander Voss explains: near a collapsed star, the Meridian passed through a field that reversed their biological time. She carries orders from the colony government — a message that can end the war brewing between Earth loyalists and colonial separatists. But she cannot remember what the message says. POV: Voss. Emotional beat: frustration and fear as her memories decay further each day.

chapters.title: The Man Who Waits
chapters.summary: Earth's Provisional Authority arrives at the vault, led by Director Cassian Rell, who claims to want to help the crew. Quentin notices Rell's soldiers carry weapons patterned on designs from the future. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: suspicion hardening into resolve as Rell's courtesy reveals itself as control.

chapters.title: Seeds and Secrets
chapters.summary: While Rell quarters his troops in the vault, Quentin secretly treats the regressing crew, learning their minds are unraveling faster than their bodies — Voss sometimes forgets she ever flew. The youngest-appearing crew member, Ensign Tam, begs Quentin to hide her. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: terror of disappearing while still alive.

chapters.title: The Message That Isn't There
chapters.summary: Rell demands the message; Voss genuinely cannot produce it. Under interrogation, fragments surface suggesting the message was never stored on the ship — it was transmitted ahead, hidden somewhere on Earth before the Meridian launched. POV: Voss. Emotional beat: humiliation giving way to a dawning, terrible hope.

chapters.title: Eleven Years of Logs
chapters.summary: Quentin reviews his own decade of broadcasts and finds anomalies: days where his logs contain phrases he never wrote, in his own voice, describing events that hadn't happened. Someone edited him across time. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: vertigo as his identity becomes evidence.

chapters.title: Rell's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Rell privately offers Quentin safety and purpose in exchange for the message, revealing Earth intends to reverse-engineer the time field as a weapon against the colonies. He frames it as mercy: better Earth holds the power than burns. POV: Rell. Emotional beat: chilling sincerity — corruption wearing the mask of protection.

chapters.title: Tam Runs
chapters.summary: Ensign Tam, now mentally a frightened teenager, flees into the ice during a supply transfer. Quentin pursues through a whiteout and saves her from the cold, earning the crew's fractured trust. Rell's men shoot at them both. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: desperate gratitude; Quentin becomes something like family.

chapters.title: The Woman in the Vault
chapters.summary: Following anomalies in his own logs, Quentin descends to the vault's sealed sublevel and finds a hidden transmitter and recordings made by Dr. Ana Reyes — the scientist he loved, who stayed behind when he thought she'd emigrated. She speaks to him across eleven years. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: heartbreak and revelation entwined.

chapters.title: Ana's Design
chapters.summary: Ana's recordings explain everything: she discovered the time-field equations years ago, foresaw the Meridian's fate, and encoded the peace message inside the only archive guaranteed to survive — and inside the memory patterns of the man who would never leave. The message is in Quentin's head. POV: Ana (recordings). Emotional beat: love as a long, patient trap and a gift.

chapters.title: Fracture
chapters.summary: Quentin begins extracting the encoded memories and suffers seizures; each recovered fragment costs him other memories — his childhood, then Ana's face. Voss helps him navigate the process using her reversed timeline as a map. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: sacrifice made visible; identity traded piece by piece.

chapters.title: Betrayal in the Greenhouse
chapters.summary: One of Rell's officers, sympathetic to the crew, warns them Rell plans to seize Quentin mid-extraction and torture the message out. The defection goes wrong; the officer dies buying them hours. POV: Voss. Emotional beat: guilt and urgency — allies are spending themselves like currency.

chapters.title: Flight Across the Ice
chapters.summary: Quentin, half-unraveled, leads Voss and Tam toward Ana's secondary transmitter in the old coastal station while Rell's forces hunt them with drones. Tam, nearly a child now, keeps them moving when Quentin collapses. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: found family forged in flight; courage without understanding.

chapters.title: The Coastal Station
chapters.summary: At the ruined station, they find Ana's second cache — and proof Rell already knew about it, meaning someone inside Ana's old circle betrayed her years ago. Rell himself arrives, alone, offering a final bargain. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: exhaustion meeting the enemy's patience.

chapters.title: Rell's Confession
chapters.summary: Rell admits he helped design the time project and that the 'war' is partly his construction — fear keeps Earth's remnant united under him. He wants the message destroyed, not delivered, because peace would dissolve his power. POV: Rell. Emotional beat: the theme made explicit; power that must keep manufacturing threats.

chapters.title: What Quentin Chooses
chapters.summary: Voss and Tam overpower Rell's escort, but Quentin realizes broadcasting the full message requires the vault's main array — back where Rell's army waits. He also realizes transmission will overwrite his remaining self entirely. He chooses to go anyway. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: quiet, terrified resolve.

chapters.title: Return to the Vault
chapters.summary: Using the seed vault's own systems and a diversion Voss flies in the crippled Meridian, Quentin infiltrates the sublevel as Rell's troops storm the ice above. Tam refuses to leave him. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: homecoming inverted — the place he preserved now preserving him for one last act.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Quentin transmits Ana's message to both worlds: proof of the time-field's true cost, recorded futures showing every faction's defeat, and Ana's plea spoken in his stolen voice. His memories burn away as the signal climbs. Rell's soldiers, hearing their own doomed tomorrows, lower their weapons. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: climax — selfhood spent like a seed, planted in everyone listening.

chapters.title: After the Signal
chapters.summary: The message spreads; Rell is arrested by his own officers. Voss, now barely remembering being a commander, tends Quentin, who retains almost nothing — not his name, not Ana. But he hums a tune Ana used to sing, and smiles at Tam. POV: Voss. Emotional beat: grief braided with tenderness; care flowing back to the caretaker.

chapters.title: First Planting
chapters.summary: Months later, Earth and the colonies negotiate openly. Voss, Tam, and a small community reopen the vault as a living garden rather than a tomb. Quentin, blank and gentle, plants seeds he doesn't remember collecting — and gets the name right anyway. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: resolution — identity outlives memory; what we tend, tends us back.
